h1: Metro Point Bangkok Hotel — 4-Star Bangkapi Steps from The Mall & MRT Yellow Line
intro: If you need a solid base in Bangkok's eastern residential belt without blowing your budget — Metro Point Bangkok Hotel is the name locals know. A 4-star property with 172 rooms sitting at the end of Soi Lat Phrao 130 since 2008 (renovated 2020), it sits just 8 minutes' walk from MRT Yellow Line's Lat Phrao 101 station, putting you within easy reach of the Ratchada-Lat Phrao junction and a transfer to the Blue Line. Add The Mall Bangkapi's dining and Harborland waterpark, street-food lanes of Serithai and Sammakorn, and a 20-minute drive to Suvarnabhumi Airport, and the hotel's appeal becomes clear for the right traveller. Score: 8.1 from 1,735 reviews on Trip.com. Rooms from approx. ฿700/night.

body.html: Metro Point Bangkok Hotel won't be splashed across luxury travel magazines, but it does something harder to find in Bangkok: it delivers clean, spacious rooms at honest prices in a neighbourhood that actually works for travellers who aren't chasing the tourist trail. The hotel opened in 2008, has operated as both a regular hotel and monthly serviced-residence ever since, and completed a renovation in 2020 that refreshed the rooms and common areas. The guest mix tells the story — you'll find business visitors on short stints, families visiting relatives in the area, and airport-transfer overnighters all under one roof.

Location deserves an honest assessment. Bangkapi is not a tourist-facing neighbourhood — it's a dense, lived-in part of eastern Bangkok — and that's precisely why rooms here cost a fraction of downtown equivalents. The MRT Yellow Line (opened 2023) has changed the maths significantly. Lat Phrao 101 station is an 8-minute walk from the hotel entrance, connecting to the Ratchada-Lat Phrao interchange and from there to the Blue Line at Sutthisan or Cultural Centre. Combine that with the Khlong Saen Saep express boat (nearby pier) for a traffic-free run into the city, and Metro Point becomes a genuinely connected base, not just a cheap sleep.
"Room is clean and spacious, close to 7-Eleven, food is very easy to find. Staff at front desk are helpful and friendly. Great value for money in this area."

Room categories run from Superior Twin (28 m²) and Deluxe Twin/Triple (35 m²) up to Metro Executive Suite (53 m²). The Deluxe rooms are the sweet spot — guests consistently describe them as larger than expected for the price, with comfortable beds, clean bathrooms, working air-conditioning, and free Wi-Fi throughout. The Executive Suite adds a separate sitting area and noticeably more breathing room, sensible for extended stays or two-person business trips. Free private parking for around 100 cars is a genuine bonus for guests arriving by car, rare and practical in this part of the city.

Facilities include the Metro Restaurant & Cafe, serving Thai and international options plus a daily breakfast buffet (6–10 AM, fee applies in most rates), and Metro Terrace, an open-air beer-garden space popular with guests for evening wind-downs. Conference and seminar rooms accommodate up to 120 people, making the hotel a local favourite for corporate events in the Bangkapi area. Room service runs 24 hours, and the front desk is staffed around the clock.

Around the hotel: The Mall Bangkapi LifeStore (with HarborLand indoor waterpark) is about 10 minutes by car. Bangkapi market and the street-food corridor along Serithai Road and Sammakorn are within the same radius. For dining beyond the hotel, the Lat Phrao 130 soi itself has a 7-Eleven immediately accessible plus several local restaurants. Suvarnabhumi Airport is roughly 20 minutes by car outside peak hours — a meaningful convenience for early-morning or late-night flights.

Honest weaknesses: reviews flag that some older rooms not yet fully renovated show their age — dated furniture, the occasional plumbing smell, or bedside lamps that need attention. Basic toiletries like toothbrushes are not always provided; bring your own. Lower-floor rooms facing the street can catch early-morning traffic noise. And no swimming pool. If any of these are deal-breakers, factor them in. But for travellers who need a clean, well-staffed, MRT-linked 4-star in Bangkapi at a fair price, Metro Point delivers consistently on its core promise — 8.1 from over 1,700 real guests backs that up.

highlights.title: MRT Yellow Line, 8 Min Walk
highlights.text: Lat Phrao 101 connects to Ratchada-Lat Phrao interchange and Blue Line transfers — no need to rely on taxis for most Bangkok trips.

highlights.title: Food & Shopping on Your Doorstep
highlights.text: 7-Eleven right on the soi, local restaurants and markets nearby, The Mall Bangkapi 10 min by car — this neighbourhood genuinely feeds you well.

highlights.text: Free private parking is a standout perk in Bangkok — a key advantage for guests driving in from the eastern suburbs or arriving from Suvarnabhumi.

honestSummary: Metro Point Bangkok Hotel is a reliable, no-nonsense 4-star base in Bangkapi — clean rooms, fair prices, friendly staff, and walking distance to the MRT Yellow Line. It won't suit travellers wanting downtown glamour or resort amenities, but for business guests, airport stopovers, and anyone needing a comfortable, well-located room in eastern Bangkok at a sensible price, it consistently delivers.
honestChecks: If you want to walk from your hotel to Siam, Ari, or Sukhumvit — Bangkapi is not the base for that. Every outing requires MRT or Grab → consider hotels nearer Ratchada or Sukhumvit instead.
If a swimming pool is non-negotiable — Metro Point has none. For families or leisure-focused stays needing pool access → look at other properties in the roundup that include this facility.
If you're concerned about room condition — request a renovated room (post-2020) when booking, or choose a higher floor, which guests report are better maintained and quieter.

tips.title: Lean on the MRT Yellow Line
tips.body: Lat Phrao 101 is an 8-minute walk away. Ride to Ratchada-Lat Phrao interchange and transfer to the Blue Line at Cultural Centre for Sukhumvit, Silom, and beyond — far cheaper and faster than Grab at peak times.

tips.title: Ask for a Renovated Room
tips.body: The hotel renovated in 2020 but not every room was upgraded simultaneously. When booking, request a recently renovated room or a higher floor — guests report these are notably cleaner and quieter.

tips.title: Explore the Neighbourhood for Food
tips.body: The soi has a 7-Eleven immediately outside, but venture a short ride to Serithai Road, Sammakorn, or the Bangkapi market for proper Thai street food at prices the hotel restaurant can't match.

tips.title: Ideal for Early or Late Flights
tips.body: Suvarnabhumi Airport is roughly 20 minutes by car from here in light traffic — significantly shorter than from downtown Bangkok. Metro Point makes a practical and affordable pre-flight or post-arrival base.

faq.q: Where is Metro Point Bangkok Hotel located and what is nearby?
faq.a: Metro Point Bangkok Hotel is at 666 Soi Lat Phrao 130 (Ramkhamhaeng 81), Bang Kapi, Bangkok 10240. It is an 8-minute walk from MRT Yellow Line Lat Phrao 101 station, roughly 10 minutes by car to The Mall Bangkapi, and about 20 minutes to Suvarnabhumi Airport.

faq.q: What are the room rates at Metro Point Bangkok Hotel?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx. ฿700/night for a Superior Twin (28 m²). Deluxe Twin/Triple (35 m²) typically ranges from ฿900–฿1,100, while the Metro Executive Suite (53 m²) is around ฿1,800. Prices vary by date and platform — compare Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Metro Point Bangkok Hotel have a swimming pool?
faq.a: No. Metro Point Bangkok Hotel does not have a swimming pool. Guests looking for pool access should check other Bangkapi hotels in our roundup that offer this facility.

faq.q: How do I get from Metro Point Bangkok Hotel to Suvarnabhumi Airport?
faq.a: The fastest option is Grab or a metered taxi — about 20 minutes in normal traffic, significantly quicker than from central Bangkok. This makes Metro Point a practical choice for early-morning or late-night flights.

faq.q: Is Metro Point Bangkok Hotel suitable for business travellers?
faq.a: Yes — it is well-suited for business guests visiting the Bangkapi-Ramkhamhaeng corridor. The hotel offers free parking, conference rooms for up to 120 people, fast Wi-Fi, and 24-hour room service. MRT Yellow Line connectivity adds to the practicality.
